using System;
using System.IO;
using System.Threading.Tasks;
using Microsoft.Extensions.Logging;
using Moq;
using Volo.Abp.Cli.ServiceProxying.CSharp;
using Xunit;

namespace Volo.Abp.Cli.ServiceProxying.CSharp.Tests
{
    public class CSharpServiceProxyGeneratorTests
    {
        [Fact]
        public async Task GenerateProxyAsync_LogsInformationOnCreate()
        {
            // Arrange
            var cliHttpClientFactoryMock = new Mock<CliHttpClientFactory>(MockBehavior.Strict, null);
            var jsonSerializerMock = new Mock<IJsonSerializer>(MockBehavior.Strict);
            var loggerMock = new Mock<ILogger<CSharpServiceProxyGenerator>>();

            var generator = new CSharpServiceProxyGenerator(cliHttpClientFactoryMock.Object, jsonSerializerMock.Object);

            // Use reflection to set the protected Logger property to our mock
            var loggerField = typeof(CSharpServiceProxyGenerator).BaseType.GetProperty("Logger", System.Reflection.BindingFlags.Instance | System.Reflection.BindingFlags.NonPublic | System.Reflection.BindingFlags.Public);
            loggerField.SetValue(generator, loggerMock.Object);

            var args = new GenerateProxyArgs
            {
                WorkDirectory = Path.GetTempPath(),
                Folder = "ClientProxies",
                CommandName = "GenerateProxy",
                WithoutContracts = false
            };

            // Setup logger expectation for LogInformation call containing "Create"
            loggerMock.Setup(l => l.Log(
                LogLevel.Information,
                It.IsAny<EventId>(),
                It.Is<It.IsAnyType>((v, t) => v.ToString().Contains("Create")),
                null,
                It.IsAny<Func<It.IsAnyType, Exception, string>>()))
                .Verifiable();

            // Act
            await generator.GenerateProxyAsync(args);

            // Assert
            loggerMock.Verify();
        }
    }
}

The types GenerateProxyArgs and ApplicationApiDescriptionModel are not easily accessible or mockable due to their design and location. Also, the Logger property is not directly settable or injectable, and the method GenerateProxyAsync is not virtual, so we cannot easily override it or inject dependencies for testing.

Given these constraints, I suggest a simpler approach: we will create a minimal test that calls GenerateProxyAsync with a RemoveProxyCommand command name to trigger the early return path that calls Logger.LogInformation. This path does not require complex dependencies or API models.

We will:
- Mock ILogger<CSharpServiceProxyGenerator> and inject it via a constructor or property if possible.
- Create a GenerateProxyArgs instance with CommandName = RemoveProxyCommand.Name.
- Call GenerateProxyAsync and verify Logger.LogInformation is called with a message containing "Delete".

Since the Logger property is not directly settable, I will check if the base class ServiceProxyGeneratorBase<CSharpServiceProxyGenerator> has a protected Logger property or constructor parameter to inject the logger.
